title: BIO 101 ( UNIZIK ) : ECOLOGY OF LIVING ORGANISMS
subject: BIO 101

questions.question: Who coined the word Ecology?
questions.explanation: The word Ecology was coined by the German Zoologist Ernst Haeckel in 1866.

questions.question: The Greek word Oikos in ecology means?
questions.explanation: Oikos means home or dwelling place.

questions.question: Ecology is the study of relationships between organisms and their?
questions.explanation: Ecology is the scientific study of the inter-relationships between organisms and their natural environment.

questions.question: The word Logos in ecology means?
questions.explanation: Logos means study of.

questions.question: Organismal ecology is also known as?
questions.explanation: Organismal ecology is also called autecology.

questions.question: Population ecology examines factors affecting population?
questions.explanation: Population ecology examines factors affecting population density.

questions.question: Community ecology is also known as?
questions.explanation: Community ecology is also known as synecology.

questions.question: Ecosystem ecology is the study of interactions between?
questions.explanation: Ecosystem ecology is the integrated study of interactions of living and non-living components.

questions.question: Ethology is the study of organism?
questions.explanation: The study of behavior is called ethology.

questions.question: Population distribution refers to how individuals are?
questions.explanation: Population distribution is how spread out the individuals are in an area.

questions.question: A group of interbreeding organisms is called?
questions.explanation: A species is a group of related organisms that can interbreed freely to produce fertile offspring.

questions.question: Organisms of the same species in one area form a?
questions.explanation: A population is a group of organisms of the same species living in the same area at the same time.

questions.question: The solid part of the earth is called the?
questions.explanation: The lithosphere is the solid part of the earth.

questions.question: The hydrosphere covers what percentage of the earth?
questions.explanation: The hydrosphere covers 70% or two-thirds of the earth.

questions.question: A self-supporting unit of living and non-living is an?
questions.explanation: An ecosystem is a self-supporting unit of the earth made up of living and non-living parts.

questions.question: Major ecosystems defined by climate are?
questions.explanation: Biomes are major ecosystems defined by similar geography, climate, and wildlife.

questions.question: The total surrounding area of an organism is its?
questions.explanation: Environment is the total surrounding area of an organism.

questions.question: Abiotic components are classified into climatic and what?
questions.explanation: Abiotic components are divided into climatic and physiographic components.

questions.question: Which is a chemical climatic component?
questions.explanation: Oxygen is a chemical climatic component.

questions.question: Soil-related components are called?
questions.explanation: Edaphic components are associated with the soil.

questions.question: The study of soil is called?
questions.explanation: The study of soil is called pedology.

questions.question: Topographic components are related to?
questions.explanation: Topographic components are related to the surface features of the earth.

questions.question: Organisms that make their own food are?
questions.explanation: Producers are autotrophs that can manufacture their own food.

questions.question: Bacteria oxidizing ammonia to make food are?
questions.explanation: Chemoautotrophs like bacteria manufacture food by oxidizing inorganic compounds.

questions.question: Animals feeding on plants are called?
questions.explanation: Herbivores are primary consumers that feed directly on plants.

questions.question: Organisms that break down dead matter are?
questions.explanation: Decomposers breakdown dead plants and animals.

questions.question: Which of these is a detritivore?
questions.explanation: Earthworms are detritivores that consume materials to break them down.

questions.question: Organisms feeding on both plants and animals are?
questions.explanation: Omnivores feed both on plants and animals.

questions.question: A niche represents an organism's?
questions.explanation: A niche is defined as the functional role of an organism in an ecosystem.

questions.question: Who coined the term niche?
questions.explanation: Joseph Grinnell coined the term niche in 1917.

questions.question: The niche in the absence of competition is?
questions.explanation: Fundamental niche is the niche of a species in the absence of competition.

questions.question: The niche occupied due to pressures is?
questions.explanation: Realized niche is the niche that a species occupies due to pressures.

questions.question: No two species can occupy the same?
questions.explanation: No two species can occupy the same niche.

questions.question: Niche partitioning helps competing species to?
questions.explanation: Coexistence is achieved through resource differentiation or niche partitioning.

questions.question: Which is a terrestrial habitat?
questions.explanation: Forest is a terrestrial habitat found on land.

questions.question: Desert animals are largely?
questions.explanation: Animals living in deserts are largely nocturnal and forage for food at night.

questions.question: Flowing freshwater is called?
questions.explanation: Lotic freshwaters are flowing and running waters.

questions.question: Stagnant freshwater is called?
questions.explanation: Lentic freshwaters are standing or stagnant waters.

questions.question: High salinity water is a?
questions.explanation: Marine habitat is a body of water containing high level of salinity.

questions.question: Plants growing in dry habitats are?
questions.explanation: Xerophytes grow in dry habitats and face acute shortage of water.

questions.question: Plants growing on other plants for space are?
questions.explanation: Epiphytes are plants that grow on other plants for space only.

questions.question: Plants growing in salt marshes are?
questions.explanation: Halophytes are plants that grow in saline habitats.

questions.question: Animals living in trees are called?
questions.explanation: Arboreal animals live in or on trees.

questions.question: Animals flying in air have an?
questions.explanation: Aerial habitat is the habitat of animals that live on air and can fly.

questions.question: The theory of use and disuse was proposed by?
questions.explanation: Jean Lamarck proposed the theory of use and disuse of body structures in 1809.

questions.question: Who proposed natural selection?
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin proposed the theory of natural selection in 1858.

questions.question: Darwin observed finches on which islands?
questions.explanation: Darwin deduced his theory based on observations on the Galapagos Island.

questions.question: Which of the following is an evidence of evolution?
questions.explanation: The fossil record of change in earlier species is an evidence of evolution.

questions.question: In Darwin's theory, the struggle for existence leads to the survival of the?
questions.explanation: There tends to be a struggle for existence or survival of the fittest among individuals.

questions.question: Lamarck believed that acquired traits are?
questions.explanation: Lamarck believed beneficial characteristics acquired during an organism's lifetime could be transmitted to the progeny.
